objective: Kubelet security: the 10250 API, anonymous authentication and Webhook authorization, the read-only port, and certificate rotation

sources.cite: CNCF KCSA Curriculum (cncf/curriculum, pinned commit 0a8cc08a): Overview of Cloud Native Security 14%, Kubernetes Cluster Component Security 22%, Kubernetes Security Fundamentals 22%, Kubernetes Threat Model 16%, Platform Security 16%, Compliance and Security Frameworks 10%
sources.note: The curriculum was read in primary text on 2026-11-07 by the course builder (backend/supabase/seed/tracks/kubernetes.ts). On 2026-11-17 a third-party summary (slauger.github.io/kubestronaut/kcsa/cluster-component-security) confirmed the 22% domain and its etcd topics (mutual TLS, access limited to the API server, encryption at rest, snapshots); the PDF itself was not re-read. The objective wording is the course seed's. Reused for REQ-336 from this course's etcd-restore-deleted-namespace-kcsa (the same reading and date); the objective wording is the course seed's.

Read 2026-11-17 with WebFetch (a summarizing fetch) of the primary page, found by WebSearch. Confirms: by default unauthenticated requests to the kubelet's HTTPS endpoint are anonymous (system:anonymous) and the default authorization mode AlwaysAllow allows every request; --anonymous-auth=false returns 401; --client-ca-file and --authentication-token-webhook (TokenReview) authenticate clients; --authorization-mode=Webhook asks the API server with SubjectAccessReview; nodes/proxy grants access to all kubelet APIs, including running commands in any container, while stats, metrics, log and spec are separate subresources.
The organization, the systems and the people are fictional. The minutes or days each step takes and the effects of each decision are teaching simplifications for exam practice, not measured values.

brief.situation: You are the security engineer at Thornbury Analytics, a fictional company running self-managed Kubernetes. A penetration test found that a Pod could list every Pod on its node through the kubelet.
handover: Kubelets run with default authentication and authorization settings.
A monitoring vendor asks for 'kubelet access' for its agent.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the map shows each component and its status in words.
Move on a check-in at a time. A decision comes to you at each check-in; before the first, you can read the evidence.
At the end you write the record and a short reflection.

then.log: Check-in 2: an attacker in a compromised web Pod lists every Pod on the node and finds a database Pod to target.
Check-in 3: an attacker uses the open kubelet's exec API to run commands in a payments container.
Check-in 4: the vendor's agent token leaks from a support bundle; with cluster-admin it reads every Secret.

choices.label: Set --anonymous-auth=false, configure --client-ca-file and --authentication-token-webhook, and make sure the API server's kubelet client certificate is set; roll it out node by node
choices.feedback: By default unauthenticated kubelet requests are anonymous; disabling it and authenticating with client certificates or tokens closes the hole.

choices.label: Leave anonymous on but firewall 10250 to the control plane
choices.feedback: Helps, but anything that gets onto an allowed network is still anonymous to the kubelet.

choices.label: Leave it: the cluster network is private
choices.feedback: Any compromised Pod can query the kubelet anonymously.

choices.label: Set --authorization-mode=Webhook so the kubelet asks the API server with SubjectAccessReview, and grant the API server's client identity the node subresources it needs
choices.feedback: Webhook mode lets RBAC decide what each client may do on the kubelet instead of allowing everything.

choices.label: Keep AlwaysAllow now that anonymous access is off
choices.feedback: Any authenticated client, however minor, can use every kubelet API.

choices.label: Turn anonymous access back on to fix a broken metrics agent, with AlwaysAllow
choices.feedback: The kubelet is open to anyone again, with every API allowed.

scoring.modelReasoning: The kubelet's API on port 10250 can list Pods and run commands. By default it treats unauthenticated requests as anonymous and authorizes everything (AlwaysAllow). Turn anonymous auth off, authenticate with client certificates or tokens, delegate authorization to the API server with Webhook mode, and grant monitoring only the metrics and stats subresources, never nodes/proxy.
